I found 13 methods in the `tokio` crate that call `trace::async_op` directly. The code-index tool answered about a different function (`async_trace_leaf`), so I searched the source for `async_op` instead. I then took the enclosing function and `impl` block for each call site.

- **`sync/rwlock.rs`:** `RwLock.read`, `RwLock.read_owned`, `RwLock.write` and `RwLock.write_owned`.
- **`sync/mutex.rs`:** `Mutex.lock` and `Mutex.lock_owned`.
- **`sync/barrier.rs`:** `Barrier.wait`.
- **`time/interval.rs`:** `Interval.tick`.
- **`sync/semaphore.rs`:** `Semaphore.acquire`, `Semaphore.acquire_many`, `Semaphore.acquire_owned` and `Semaphore.acquire_many_owned`.
- **`sync/oneshot.rs`:** `Sender.closed`.

Some other files only use the `"runtime.resource.async_op"` span name as a string and don't call the function, so I left them out. Those are `batch_semaphore.rs`, `sleep.rs`, `oneshot.rs` (`Receiver`) and the tracing tests.
